copy.gary: I've been wandering Asheville parks and I still find something new on most visits, like the long view from Beaucatcher Overlook or a quiet stretch of the French Broad River Greenway.
copy.description: Check in at every Asheville, North Carolina park you visit, collect stamps and badges, rate your favorites and explore with your Park Pals.

motifs.name: Land of the Sky
motifs.blurb: Asheville sits in a bowl of the Blue Ridge Mountains, which is how it earned the nickname Land of the Sky.

motifs.name: The French Broad
motifs.blurb: The French Broad River, often called one of the oldest rivers in the world, runs north through the city past its riverfront parks.

motifs.name: City Hall
motifs.blurb: Asheville's 1928 Art Deco City Hall, by architect Douglas Ellington, rises in stepped tiers under a pink and green roof.

motifs.name: The drum circle
motifs.blurb: On warm Friday evenings a drum circle gathers in Pritchard Park, and anyone can join in or dance.

motifs.name: The Edible Park
motifs.blurb: Dr. George Washington Carver Edible Park is one of the country's first public food forests: pick the fruit and nuts as you walk.

motifs.name: Carrier Park velodrome
motifs.blurb: Carrier Park was once the Asheville Motor Speedway. Today its old track is a velodrome for bikes, skates and walkers.

motifs.name: Riverside's writers
motifs.blurb: Riverside Cemetery is the resting place of two great writers: Asheville's own Thomas Wolfe and the short story master O. Henry.

motifs.name: The Urban Trail
motifs.blurb: The Asheville Urban Trail is a walk through downtown history, with sculptures and plaques at each stop.
